item.description: Automated hospitality services raise questions about transparency when guests first encounter artificial intelligence (AI) and when systems cannot resolve their requests. item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming scientific research, environmental sustainability, healthcare, and intelligent infrastructure. item.description: Technology Research and Development and the Making of the EU’s Borders poses the question of how the Research and Development (R&D) of border security technologies constitutes a political practice of border security. item.description: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. item.title: Who benefits from LLMs? Prompt engineering competence and equity in higher education
item.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly becoming embedded in higher education, yet their benefits may be unevenly distributed. This study conceptualizes prompt engineering competence (PEC) as an equity-relevant interaction competence and examines whether differences in PEC are associated with perceived academic gains and perceived educational inequity.
